content: Two identical non-conducting solid spheres of same mass and charge are suspended in air from a common point by two non-conducting, massless strings of same length. At equilibrium, the angle between the strings is <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: -0.025ex;" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1.448ex" height="1.025ex" role="img" focusable="false" viewBox="0 -442 640 453" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g data-mml-node="math"><g data-mml-node="mi"><use data-c="1D6FC" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-I-1D6FC"></use></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container>. The spheres are now immersed in a dielectric liquid of density 800 kg m<sup><mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: -0.186ex;" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1.76ex" height="1.505ex" role="img" focusable="false" viewBox="0 -583 778 665" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g data-mml-node="math"><g data-mml-node="mo"><use data-c="2212" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-N-2212"></use></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container>3</sup> and dielectric constant 21. If the angle between the strings remains the same after the immersion, then

options.content: electric force between the spheres remains unchanged
electric force between the spheres reduces

mass density of the spheres is 840 kg m<sup><mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: -0.186ex;" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1.76ex" height="1.505ex" role="img" focusable="false" viewBox="0 -583 778 665" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g data-mml-node="math"><g data-mml-node="mo"><use data-c="2212" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-N-2212"></use></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container>3</sup>
the tension in the strings holding the spheres remains unchanged

explanation:
In air,



T cos = mg ..... (i)

T sin = qE ..... (ii)

qE = mg tan ..... (iii)

In liquid,



T' cos = mg U

T' cos = mg - vg ..... (iv)

T' sin = ...... (v)

Dividing Eq. (v) by Eq. (ii), we get

..... (vi)

Dividing Eq. (iv) by Eq. (v), we get

(mg - vg)tan

K(mg - vg)tan ..... (vii)

From Eqs. (vii) and (iii), we get

mg tan = K(mg - vg)tan

m = K(m - v)

dv = K(dv - v)

d = Kd - K

d = 21d - 21 [ K = 21]

20d = 21

20d = 21 800

d = 840 kg/m3
